meta.name: experimental-design
meta.description: Design experiments and studies BEFORE data is collected — choosing a design, randomizing, blocking, and laying out treatment combinations so results are interpretable. Use whenever someone is planning a study, asks how to assign subjects/samples to groups, mentions randomization, blocking, stratification, controls, factorial or fractional-factorial designs, design of experiments (DOE), screening many factors, response-surface optimization, crossover or repeated-measures or split-plot designs, cluster/group randomization, Latin squares, plate layouts, batch/run-order effects, replication vs. pseudoreplication, or sequential/adaptive/group-sequential designs. Trigger even for informal phrasings like "how should I set up this experiment", "how do I avoid confounding", "what's the best way to test these 6 factors", or "assign these mice to conditions". For computing the sample size or power once the design is chosen, use statistical-power; for analyzing data already collected, use statistical-analysis.

copy.tagline_en: Design rigorous experiments that yield trustworthy conclusions
copy.fit_line_en: For you if you are planning an experiment and unsure about group assignment and randomization.

howto.what: 在你收集数据之前,帮你选定合适的实验设计,生成可复现的随机分组或 DOE 试验排布(可导出 CSV),并指出伪重复、混杂等结构性问题。
howto.when: 当你在计划研究、要把受试对象或样本分配到各组,或提到随机化、区组等关键词时接管;像「这个实验该怎么搭」这样的口语提问也会触发。

howto.what_en: Before data is collected, it helps pick an experimental design and generates a reproducible randomization or DOE layout (exportable to CSV), flagging structural problems such as pseudoreplication and confounding.
howto.when_en: Triggers when you plan a study, assign subjects or samples to groups, or mention randomization, blocking, and similar terms, including informal asks like "how should I set up this experiment".

say_en.text: Randomize 60 mice into treatment and control using blocked randomization
Screen 7 factors with a Plackett-Burman design
say_en.note: Returns the run matrix in real units

say_en.text: Check this experiment for pseudoreplication or confounding
